meta: Hendrick Avercamp's Winter Landscape with Skaters, painted around 1608 and bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1897.
about: Skaters and sledgers cross a frozen river beside a village of brick houses and a church tower, while villagers go about their chores and a dog chews a carcass at the lower left. Fishermen in the foreground work to free a frozen sailboat. A wooden bird trap stands at the left. Hendrick Avercamp painted it around 1608, and it is counted among his earliest works. The bird trap and the style recall Pieter Bruegel the Elder's winter scenes. Avercamp signed it as graffiti on the fisherman's hut. The Rijksmuseum acquired it in 1897 with help from the Vereniging Rembrandt.

meta: Pietro Longhi's The Game of the Cooking Pot, a blindfolded game among elegant Venetians, given to the National Gallery of Art in 1939.
about: A blindfolded man with a stick faces a clay pot on the floor in a richly furnished room, while elegantly dressed onlookers watch. A woman in a white gown holds a fan near a young man in gold-embroidered clothes. Pietro Longhi painted The Game of the Cooking Pot. Prince Alberto Giovanelli of Venice owned it first. Count Alessandro Contini Bonacossi in Rome then handled it, and the Kress Foundation bought it in 1931 and gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1939.

meta: Ike Taiga's hanging scroll Night Mooring at Maple Bridge, which carries a poem by the Chinese poet Zhang Ji.
about: Ike Taiga inscribed a poem by the Chinese poet Zhang Ji at the upper left of this hanging scroll. It describes a traveler's uneasy sleep after the moon has set, with crows cawing, frost in the sky, a riverside maple and fishing lights, and the midnight bell of Hanshan Temple carrying across to his boat. The painting follows the poem. A traveler's boat appears through dense foliage in the foreground, a maple and two fishing boats stand in the middle ground, and Hanshan Temple lies in the distance. The Cleveland Museum of Art dates the scroll to the mid to late 1700s.

meta: Pieter Jansz Saenredam's 1637 view of the transept of the Mariakerk in Utrecht, with visitors and beggars on crutches.
about: The transept of the Mariakerk in Utrecht is seen from the northeast, with tall stone piers, arched vaults and tall windows letting in soft light. A few visitors and beggars stand in the foreground, and some of the beggars use crutches. Small figures walk across the patterned stone floor. Pieter Saenredam signed the painting at the upper left and added Pinxit Anno 1637, Latin for painted in the year 1637.

meta: Balthasar van der Ast's Basket of Fruits, a still life probably owned by Princess Amalia van Solms and given to the National Gallery of Art in 1992.
about: A wicker basket heaped with grapes, plums, apricots and quinces sits on a blue and white porcelain dish, with loose fruit, cherries on a twig and vine leaves spread across the grey table in front. Balthasar van der Ast painted it. The National Gallery of Art says it was probably in the collection of Princess Amalia van Solms in The Hague, where an inventory of 1632 lists it. It was sold with a companion piece in Amsterdam in 1802. Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon later bought it, and they gave it to the museum in 1992.
dimensions:
painted surface: 18.1 x 22.8 cm (7 1/8 x 9 in.)
overall (with additions): 18.8 x 23.5 cm (7 3/8 x 9 1/4 in.)
framed: 38.4 x 43.8 x 3.2 cm (15 1/8 x 17 1/4 x 1 1/4 in.)

meta: A painting of David with the head of Goliath, identified as the work of Artemisia Gentileschi in 2020 by her name on the sword blade.
about: David sits with dark curly hair, one hand on the gold hilt of a long sword and his bare feet near a severed head. It was identified as the work of Artemisia Gentileschi only in 2020, after the art historian Gianni Papi and conservators at Simon Gillespie Studio found her name painted along the blade of David's sword. Before that it was attributed to Giovanni Francesco Guerrieri, a student of her father Orazio. Recent research suggests it was once part of the collection of Charles I.

meta: Dirk Stoop's Hunters Resting, a 1645 landscape with three hunters, their dogs and a rider blowing a horn.
about: Three hunters rest with their dogs in a hilly landscape, and a rider at the left blows his hunting horn. At the right a horse relieves itself on the dirt path. A rocky bank with autumn trees rises beneath a warm, cloud-filled sky. Dirk Stoop painted the scene, which the Rijksmuseum dates to 1645, and signed it at the bottom right with a signature that is partly illegible.

meta: Lucien Pissarro's 1921 painting of apple blossom at Riversbridge Farm, Blackpool, in the Devon valley he first visited in 1913.
about: A spring orchard in full blossom, with pale pink and white flowers on the branches in front and a farmhouse with red chimneys among green fields and wooded hills. Lucien Pissarro painted Apple Blossom, Riversbridge Farm, Blackpool in 1921. The Royal Albert Memorial Museum describes him as a founder member of the Camden Town Group whose main interest in Devon was Blackpool Vale, some four miles south west of Dartmouth. He first visited in 1913 to recover from illness and returned later. He called his landscapes little corners which compose harmoniously.

meta: Marco Ricci's An Opera Rehearsal, with Horace Walpole's note on its back crediting the figures to Sebastiano Ricci.
about: Horace Walpole wrote on a label on the back that he bought this picture at the sale of John, Duke of Argyll, in March 1771. He doubted that Hogarth painted it. The singers were earlier than Hogarth's picture, he said, as the dresses of Queen Anne's late reign show. Signora Margherita is the woman in black. Walpole judged it certainly the work of Sebastiano Ricci, with the landscape by Marco Ricci. A wigged conductor in a gold waistcoat gestures toward musicians with a cello, double bass and harpsichord.

meta: Frank Myers Boggs's 1883 moonlit painting On the Thames, one of many views of the river by the American painter.
about: Dark-sailed barges move across a calm grey river under a moon half veiled by cloud, with a distant skyline and smoke rising from chimneys. Small rowboats dot the water. Frank Myers Boggs, an American painter, made this oil on canvas in 1883. It was one of numerous paintings of the River Thames that he produced. He operated an art studio on the river's bank in London. The painting is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

meta: François-Thomas Mondon's 1730 chinoiserie print of a fantastical garden with a many-faced figure on a shell throne.
about: A male figure with three faces and four arms sits on a shell throne at the top of a large rocaille structure with steps, a balustrade, arches and a water feature below. A banner flies to the right, trees stand in the background, and a figure and a bird appear in the foreground. The Cooper Hewitt describes the plate as a chinoiserie ornament print, a European style inspired by fanciful ideas of China and East Asia. François-Thomas Mondon made it in 1730. The plate is numbered and signed.

meta: Gottfried Engelmann's neoclassical plate of friezes and ornamental borders from 1820, once titled as a set of designs by Dubois.
about: Four friezes run across the top of this sheet, with a motif for a fifth, and three more friezes fill the bottom. Neoclassical ornament in black and white includes swans flanking an urn of fruit, scrolling acanthus, rosettes and fluted columns. The sheet is labeled Pl. 3. The Cooper Hewitt notes that it was previously titled Plate 3 of a set of projects for ornaments devised by Dubois, and that the right and bottom edges are creased and stained. Gottfried Engelmann is credited with the design, dated 1820.

meta: Pieter de Hooch's The Bedroom, a domestic interior with a child at the door, later owned by Peter A. B. Widener.
about: A small child stands at an open door while a woman in a white cap and red bodice folds fabric near a bed. The floor is tiled. Pieter de Hooch painted The Bedroom. Hofstede de Groot, who catalogued it in the early twentieth century, called it similar in all respects to the picture at Karlsruhe, except that the little mirror by the bed has no ornament at top and bottom. He listed its sales: Stinstra in Amsterdam in 1822 at 25 florins, Lord Radstock in London at 70 guineas, and Adrian Hope in London in 1894 at 2,257 pounds. It later belonged to Peter A. B. Widener.

meta: John Wesley Jarvis's portrait of Commodore John Rodgers in naval uniform, painted around 1814 and given to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.
about: Commodore John Rodgers tucks one hand into his dark blue naval coat, which has gold epaulettes and brass buttons, with a stormy sea and two sailing ships behind him. John Wesley Jarvis painted the portrait around 1814. In 1838 Charlotte I. Bullus of New York gave it to Rodgers's widow, Minerva Denison Rodgers, in Washington. It then went to her daughter Ann Minerva Rodgers Macomb and on to Ann's two daughters, who gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.
credit_line: Gift of Nannie R. and Christina Macomb

meta: Samuel F. B. Morse's The House of Representatives, a view of the chamber in 1822 that he toured in 1823 and the National Gallery of Art acquired in 2014.
about: Rows of dark-suited men sit at desks and stand in conversation under a coffered dome, with marble columns and red draperies between them. Samuel Morse painted a session of the United States House of Representatives in a chamber designed by Benjamin Henry Latrobe, now the National Statuary Hall. Morse was an inventor as well as a painter. He signed the canvas in 1822 and exhibited it in several cities in 1823, drawing critical praise but making little money. Charles Robert Leslie in London owned it by 1828. The National Gallery of Art acquired it in 2014.

meta: Hendrick ter Brugghen's Bagpipe Player, restituted to its heirs in 2008 and bought by the National Gallery of Art in 2009.
about: A man in profile plays a bagpipe, his cheek and lips pressed to the mouthpiece while an arm grips the bag, and the pipes rest over his shoulder. He wears a loose white shirt and a dark cap against a plain warm background. An inventory of Aernout van Lingen in Utrecht in 1676 lists a bagpipe by Ter Brugghen, which may be this one. The Wallraf-Richartz-Museum in Cologne acquired it, but restituted it in 2008 to the heirs of its earlier owner Klemperer, and the National Gallery of Art bought it in 2009.
credit_line: Paul Mellon Fund and Greg and Candy Fazakerley Fund

meta: Willem Kalf's Still Life with a bowl of peaches, once in the Havemeyer collection and later given by Chester Dale.
about: Peaches, an orange and a spiral lemon peel fill a blue and white bowl on a draped table, with a fluted glass flask and a stemmed wine glass behind. A sprig with a small white blossom lies nearby. Willem Kalf painted it. Cottier and Company in New York sold it in 1889 to Louisine Havemeyer, and it came up at the American Art Association in New York in 1930. Chester Dale bought it and gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1943.

meta: László Moholy-Nagy's 1922 constructivist oil painting E IV, held by the Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe.
about: A black circle, a pale gray crescent and several thin diagonal bands in red and yellow float against a dark gray ground. The Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe calls László Moholy-Nagy, a Hungarian-born painter, photographer and typographer, one of the leading figures of Constructivism. It describes E IV, also known as Konstruktion VII, as an exemplary example of that movement and a characteristic work of the artist. He painted it in oil on canvas in 1922.

meta: Jean-Charles Cazin's view of a stone quarry near Nanterre, owned by Ian M. Cumming and bequeathed to the National Gallery of Art in 2021.
about: Workers cut and haul pale stone blocks in a terraced quarry, where two horses pull a cart along the stepped excavation. A man in a dark coat and hat stands in the foreground beside cut blocks. Jean-Charles Cazin signed the canvas at lower right. It belonged to a H. Lyon, possibly the dealer Henry Lyon, before a Christie's sale in London in 1954. After a second Christie's sale, Ian M. Cumming bought it in 1992, and his estate bequeathed it to the National Gallery of Art in 2021.
credit_line: Gift of Ian and Annette Cumming

meta: Giuseppe Maria Crespi's Tarquin and Lucretia, long sold as a work by Mattia Preti before it reached the National Gallery of Art.
about: A man in a gold-trimmed tunic and bare feet presses his hand to the head of a woman who gazes upward, her throat and shoulder bare. A dagger lies on the floor near a fallen pink rose petal. Giuseppe Maria Crespi painted Tarquin and Lucretia, but for a long time it carried another name. Duke Albert of Saxe-Teschen probably had it by 1768 as a work by Mattia Preti, and it was sold as Preti again in Brussels in 1833. The Kress Foundation gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1952.

meta: James Peale's portrait of General Horatio Gates, the American commander honored for the surrender at Saratoga.
about: Horatio Gates, shown in a dark blue military coat with gold epaulettes against a cloudy sky, was born in Maldon, England. He fought in the French and Indian War and rose to major before peace ended his advancement. After he moved to North America he bought a plantation in present-day West Virginia in 1773 and enslaved laborers to work it. Congress gave him a gold medal for the surrender of General Burgoyne's army at Saratoga in 1777. His reputation was ruined by his defeat at Camden in 1780, a retreat that Alexander Hamilton mocked as admirable activity in a man of his age.

meta: Sakai Hoitsu's hanging scroll Moon and Autumn Plants, painted in 1800 with a hazy moon behind morning glories and grasses.
about: A pale full moon hangs behind clusters of autumn plants on this hanging scroll, among them white morning glory blossoms, blue flowers and feathery grasses. Moon and autumn plants was a popular subject for Sakai Hoitsu, and close variations exist as single paintings and as parts of larger sets showing the birds and flowers of the twelve months. The museum says his observation of nature comes close to botanical drawing but keeps a delicate, gossamer quality. He gets that balance by building forms from layered washes of pigment, with no ink outline. The scroll is dated 1800.

meta: Jan Lutma's 1630 design for an ewer in the auricular style, with a merman handle and a kneeling merman as its shaft.
about: An ewer in the auricular style is drawn in profile, though its uppermost part is missing. The handle is a merman with, it seems, a mermaid leaning back toward him. Two panels with reliefs of children flank the body, and the relief on the left forms the shape of a mouth. A kneeling merman supports the body like an Atlas. Jan Lutma made the design in 1630, as the Cooper Hewitt dates it.

meta: Moretto da Brescia's 1518 painting of Christ carrying the cross before a kneeling figure, once wrongly attributed to Titian.
about: Christ, draped in red cloth, bears a tall wooden cross and looks upward while a kneeling figure appears before him. Moretto da Brescia painted it in 1518. It is first recorded in 1859, in the collection of Guglielmo Lochis, when it was wrongly attributed to Titian. No earlier owners are known. A study in 1886 restored the attribution to Moretto and dated the painting to his youth. It is now in the Accademia Carrara in Bergamo.

meta: Willem de Famars Testas's 1868 painting of the courtyard of a house in Cairo, with a veiled mother, a child and a man with a horse.
about: In the doorway of an old house in Cairo, a veiled mother with a child talks to a man with a horse, and a few children look on. A wooden mashrabiya window projects above the carved stone doorway. Willem de Famars Testas painted the courtyard in 1868 and signed it at lower left as W. Testas.

meta: The middle panel of Gerard David's Saint Anne Altarpiece, showing Saint Anne with the Virgin and Child, later owned by Peter A. B. Widener.
about: Saint Anne sits enthroned in a red mantle and white veil, holding an open book that the Christ Child reaches toward, while the Virgin Mary sits beside her in blue. Carved cherubs stand on the pillars. A band around the Virgin's forehead carries a Latin inscription that calls her mother of grace. Cardinal Antonio Despuig y Dameto had the panel at Raxa on Mallorca, and it passed to the Counts of Montenegro. Leon de Somzée in Brussels owned it by 1899. Peter A. B. Widener of Pennsylvania bought it in 1907, and his family gave it to the National Gallery of Art in 1942.
dimensions:
painted surface (including addition at top): 232.5 x 96 cm (91 9/16 x 37 13/16 in.)
overall (panel): 236.1 x 97.5 cm (92 15/16 x 38 3/8 in.)

meta: Hishikawa Moronobu's hanging scroll of a beauty turning her head, by the artist credited as the first true ukiyo-e master.
about: A standing woman with long dark hair and a small white hair ornament turns her head and raises a hand to her shoulder. She wears a pale green kimono patterned with pink and blue blossoms. Hishikawa Moronobu rarely painted single beauties like this one. The Art Institute of Chicago credits him as the first true artist of ukiyo-e, or floating world pictures, and says he was known for scenes of common people's leisure, including visits to the Yoshiwara pleasure quarters. He came from Awa province, moved into the city by the 1670s and worked as a book illustrator and print designer before turning to scrolls.
dimensions: 70.6 × 26.5 cm (27 × 10 in.); With mounting: 151.1 × 38.1 cm (59 1/2 × 15 in.); Width including lower roller: W.: 43.2 cm (17 in.)

meta: Jan Stolker's 1757 family portrait of Theodorus Bisdom van Vliet, mayor of Haastrecht, on a garden terrace with his wife and children.
about: Theodorus Bisdom van Vliet sits with his family on a terrace in the garden of his house at Haastrecht, in front of a statue of Neptune and Mercury. The Rijksmuseum identifies him as mayor of Haastrecht and a water board official of the Krimpenerwaard. With him are his wife Maria van Harthals and their children, one of whom, Johan de Wijs, plays a flute. Jan Stolker signed and dated it 1757. It was commissioned by or for the sitters and stayed in the family for generations.

meta: Frédéric Bazille's portrait of the writer and librettist Édouard Blau, later owned by Chester Dale.
about: A man with dark wavy hair and a mustache sits in a green upholstered chair with red trim, wearing a dark coat, waistcoat and white collar. He is the French writer and librettist Édouard Blau. Frédéric Bazille signed the canvas at upper left and dated it 1866, though the museum's catalogue says probably 1869. The Leicester Galleries in London sold it to Chester Dale, who left it to the National Gallery of Art in 1963.

meta: Jacob Esselens's 1650 view of the beach seen from the dunes, with a couple buying fish from a seller.
about: Seen from the dunes, the beach has a man and a woman buying fish from a seller in the foreground. At the right a horse and cart and a few fishing boats stand on the sand. Heavy clouds fill the pale sky above a flat shoreline. Jacob Esselens signed it at lower right with the name JEsselens, and the Rijksmuseum dates it to 1650.

meta: Utagawa Toyohiro's hanging scroll of a fashionable woman by the Mimeguri Shrine on the Sumida River in Tokyo.
about: A fashionable woman enjoys a cool evening by the Mimeguri Shrine, on an embankment of the Sumida River in Tokyo. Her clothing advertises her sophistication: a chic lightweight black kimono that lets the colors of her robes show through, with a matching obi. She glances back over her shoulder on a stone path while a tree rises at left. Utagawa Toyohiro belonged to the second generation of the Utagawa School, the most prominent painters of ukiyo-e. The Art Institute of Chicago dates the scroll to the Bunka era, about 1804 to 1818.
dimensions: 70.5 × 26.5 cm (27 3/4 × 10 7/16 in.); Mounting: 158.1 × 37.2 cm (62 1/4 × 14 5/8 in.); Width including lower roller: W.: 42.6 cm (16 3/4 in.)

meta: Jan Asselijn's sunset view of the Ponte Molle over the Tiber, once in the Hague collection of Willem Lormier.
about: The Ponte Molle crosses the Tiber at sunset as a long arched bridge, with a round tower and a ruined tower draped in vegetation on the right. Herders drive cattle through the shallows while a man rows a boat. Jan Asselijn signed the canvas with a monogram. It was owned by the Hague collector Willem Lormier, whose catalogue of 1752 guided visitors to his 376 paintings, and was sold at his estate sale in 1763. Yves Gottfried Winkler of Leipzig later owned it. The National Gallery of Art purchased it from the Tydeman family in 2012.
credit_line: Florian Carr Fund, New Century Fund, and Nell and Robert Weidenhammer Fund

meta: George Caleb Bingham's The Jolly Flatboatmen, bought in 1846 by the American Art-Union and engraved as a mezzotint.
about: Men aboard a wooden flatboat on a calm river relax and celebrate, with one man dancing with arms raised while a fiddler plays nearby. George Caleb Bingham sent the picture to the American Art-Union in New York, whose committee recommended buying it in October 1846 under the name Dance on the Flat boat. The Union chose it to be engraved as a mezzotint and renamed it The Jolly Flatboatman that December. It awarded the painting at its annual meeting in 1847 to Benjamin van Schaick. Later it belonged to Herbert Claiborne Pell Jr. and his son Claiborne Pell.

meta: Egbert Lievensz. van der Poel's 1640 fish market at night, lit by a large lantern.
about: A seated woman sells fish from behind a stall by the light of a large lantern. A big salmon lies on the table, baskets of fish stand in front, and a woman with a bucket on her arm is buying. The sails of a barge show at the left in the background. Egbert van der Poel signed the picture on a column at the center, and the Rijksmuseum dates it to 1640.

meta: Francesco Hayez's Pietro Rossi, a Romantic history painting of a knight asked to lead the Venetian army against the Scaligeri.
about: Francesco Hayez painted Pietro Rossi between 1818 and 1820. A version is in the San Fiorano collection in Milan, and a copy is in the Pinacoteca di Brera. Both show Rossi accepting, through a messenger, an invitation from Francesco Dandolo to command the Venetian resistance to the expansionist Scaligeri. An armored knight stands at center with a sword while kneeling women and a young man gather around him. When it was first exhibited at the Brera in 1820 it won great acclaim for its medieval subject and the drama of its dark, shadowy palette.

meta: Paulus Constantijn la Fargue's 1756 view of the turning basin of the towpath canal at Leidschendam, bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1998.
about: Three towing barges lie in the turning basin of the towpath canal between The Hague and Leiden at Leidschendam. A hunter with a horse walks on the quay among travelers and walkers at the left, near the Reformed Church on the Delft quay. In the distance stands a small house belonging to the country house Damlust. Paulus Constantijn la Fargue signed it in 1756. The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1998 for 45,000 guilders, after it had been sold in 1989 as the work of a follower.

meta: Sano di Pietro's tempera panel of the Virgin and Child with saints and a Crucifixion, with its back painted to look like porphyry.
about: Sano di Pietro painted this panel in the 1400s in tempera and gold, with the Virgin and Child adored by Saints Mary Magdalene and Nicholas of Bari, and a Crucifixion with the Virgin and Saint John. The painter did not leave the back plain. According to the Cleveland Museum of Art, he covered the sides and reverse with a thin layer of gesso and left the texture of the rough wood visible. He then painted it to look like porphyry, a valuable stone.
credit_line: Gift of Mrs. B. P. Bole, Mr. and Mrs. Guerdon S. Holden, Mrs. Windsor T. White, and the L. E. Holden Fund

meta: Vittore Carpaccio's Madonna and Child on a poplar panel, once owned by a lawyer in Marseilles and given by the Kress Foundation in 1961.
about: The Virgin sits in a red gown and blue mantle, holding an open book while the Christ Child rests on her lap and two winged cherub heads hover in the sky. Vittore Carpaccio painted the Madonna and Child on a poplar panel in the early 1500s. A Mr. Nathan of Marseilles, head of the bar there, owned it, though Georges Wildenstein later said he did not know where Nathan got it. Wildenstein sold it to the Kress Foundation in 1954. Kress records say it was restored in Italy by G. Marchig about 1952.

meta: Joseph Nash the Elder's 1870 watercolor of an Elizabethan room at Lyme Hall, Cheshire, a style revived in the Victorian period.
about: A woman in black plays a lute beside a child in a richly decorated Elizabethan room with a carved stone fireplace, leaded stained glass windows and carved oak paneling. Joseph Nash the Elder made the watercolor of a room at Lyme Hall, Cheshire, in 1870. The Cooper Hewitt says the Elizabethan interior was a popular style revived in the Victorian period, marked by heavily carved panelling, stained glass, plasterwork and high-backed carved oak chairs. An armorial cartouche on the overmantel and a gold ewer and tray on a skirted table are elements commonly seen in such rooms.

meta: Worthington Whittredge's Second Beach, Newport, a sweeping shoreline owned by Thomas Barlow Walker and bought by the National Gallery of Art in 2004.
about: Gentle surf curls along a broad sandy beach, with a large rocky outcrop on the left and small figures wading and strolling near the water. Worthington Whittredge painted Second Beach at Newport. Thomas Barlow Walker of Minneapolis owned it, and his foundation gave it to the Walker Art Center in 1976. It was sold at Sotheby's in New York in 1989 and passed to Juliana Terian. The National Gallery of Art purchased it through David Nisinson Fine Art in 2004.
credit_line: Paul Mellon Fund and Gift of Juliana Terian in memory of Peter G. Terian

meta: Leonardo da Vinci's Annunciation, his earliest surviving major work, painted in Verrocchio's workshop and in the Uffizi since 1867.
about: Leonardo da Vinci painted this Annunciation in oil and tempera on a large poplar panel while he was an apprentice in the studio of Andrea del Verrocchio in Florence. A winged angel kneels on a flowery lawn and holds out a white lily, and the Virgin sits before a marble lectern with an open book. Wikipedia dates the work to about 1472 to 1476 and calls it his earliest surviving major work. It has been in the Uffizi since 1867, though it has been criticized for inaccuracies in its composition.
